meta.description: External reference fixtures for the Merton (1974) structural credit model (KMV equity inversion, distance to default, default probability, endogenous debt spread), the Black-Cox (1976) first-passage default probability, and Merton (1976) jump-diffusion European prices.

reference_source.name: MATLAB mertonmodel documentation; Hull (2022) Example 24.3; QuantLib (Python)

extra.equity_inversion: Hull (2022), Example 24.3 (inputs, as cited by the replication); expected values from the independent Newton solve in gen_merton_golden.py, cross-checked against the R replication at https://mlozanoqf.github.io/tutorial_arf/02-merton.html
extra.jump_series: Merton, R. (1976), Option pricing when underlying stock returns are discontinuous, JFE 3

conventions.rates: continuously compounded annual decimals, including payout rates and dividend yields
conventions.time: year fractions; QuantLib dates are whole 365-day years under Actual/365 Fixed
conventions.valuation_date: none: every model input is a year fraction. QuantLib evaluation date 2026-01-15 only anchors its flat term structures
conventions.units: asset, equity and debt values share one currency unit; volatilities, rates, spreads and probabilities are decimals; option prices are per unit of underlying
conventions.kmv_published: debt barrier = Liability; DD and PD use the physical Drift; Maturity 1 year
conventions.equity_inversion: E = V e^{-qT} N(d1) - B e^{-rT} N(d2), sigma_E = N(d1) e^{-qT} sigma_V V / E; DD and PD are risk-neutral (d2, N(-d2)); debt spread = -ln((V e^{-qT} - E)/(B e^{-rT}))/T. The payout terms follow this crate's documented convention; only the payout_rate = 0 cases are externally anchored
conventions.black_cox: risk-neutral probability that V_t touches B e^{g t} before T, continuous monitoring
conventions.jump: dS/S = (r - q - lambda k) dt + sigma dW + (J - 1) dN, ln J ~ N(mu_jump, sigma_jump^2), k = exp(mu_jump + sigma_jump^2/2) - 1; discounted prices per unit of underlying

tolerances.kmv_published: half a unit of the last printed digit: 5e-5 for volatility, DD and PD (4 decimals), 500 for asset value (5 significant figures at 1e7 scale)
tolerances.equity_inversion: 1e-6 relative: the reference is converged to 1e-13; the production fixed point stops at a 1e-8 relative step
tolerances.black_cox: 5e-9 absolute: the crate's adjudicated closed-form tolerance against QuantLib's normal CDF (see vol_models_quantlib)
tolerances.jump_bates_limit: 1e-7 relative: QuantLib's own Bates-vs-Merton tolerance is 2e-8, widened for the 128-term COS expansion
tolerances.jump_quantlib_table: 1e-2 absolute: the tolerance QuantLib applies to this table, whose values are printed to 2 decimals
tolerances.jump_series: 1e-6 absolute: an a priori bound equal to the one this crate's COS-vs-Black-Scholes unit tests assert for the default 128-term expansion
